_comment: Where jacksonheights' data wells are. Shape: cartograph/sources.js; the wells themselves live in the state record (cartograph/states/ny.mjs), where New York City is a sub-state jurisdiction (BRIEF-nyc-adapter). Declared BEFORE the first fetch, so Extent's fetch is NYC-aware from the start: its building identity seals on the city's BIN, not on Microsoft's centroids.
_jurisdiction: Jackson Heights, Queens, New York City — Queens Community District 3 (BoroCD 403). Web address jacksonheights (jacksonheights.online; Jacob, 2026-10-05). NYC's wells are citywide; the fetch envelope scopes them, so the town selects nothing.
_landUseCodes_why: PLUTO's LandUse (01–11) is read by the state's own vocabulary (states/ny.mjs#readNycPlutoLandUse); there is no decode table to fetch.
_buildings_why: NYC publishes its own building footprints, each with a permanent BIN; on an NYC town they ARE the geometry well and Microsoft's are not fetched (footprint-well.mjs). OSM still unions in.
_trees_why: NYC Parks' live Forestry inventory and the 2015 Street Tree Census, unioned; the live survey's removal records supersede a 2015 tree within DEDUP_M (Jacob, 2026-10-06: 'we want to be most up to date'). Standing dead trees are kept on record, not planted.

tide.why: Worlds Fair Marina, on Flushing Bay — the water this envelope touches; no CO-OPS station lies inside the bbox (Jacob, 2026-10-05)

_cropland_why: USDA's national Cropland Data Layer (cartograph/cdl.mjs), declared like every US town (what it reads in Queens is not yet measured).
